note: LLM generation results for the NVIDIA N1X (RTX Spark) laptops; every value with the URL it was read from. id = position in this list, used by n1xllm.py. x is decode tokens/s. Only row 0 carries power measured with the run (whole laptop on battery, read by Windows and checked against the battery drain); n1xllm.py borrows power for the others from the same laptop model's Cyberpunk 2077 wall power already on the page. No GB10 (DGX Spark) value is used for the N1X.

rows.quant: 4-bit ("Modèles quantifiés en 4 bits"; the GGUF type is not named), 22 GB file
rows.test: 30 consecutive 1,024-token answers (about 7 minutes of continuous generation), on battery, Asus Performance mode, 85 GiB reserved for the GPU
rows.device: Asus ProArt P16 with the RTX Spark N1X, 128 GB, 99.9 Wh battery, Windows 11 on Arm, driver 617.42
rows.power: "En génération continue avec Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, mesurée entre 92 et 30 % de batterie, le ProArt P16 tire 89 à 93 W et perd environ 1,56 % de batterie par minute, tout en écrivant 72 tok/s"; "la RTX Spark consomme 0,36 Wh pour 1 000 tokens écrits"; "La puissance des deux PC est lue par Windows". 1.56%/min of 99.9 Wh is 93.5 W; 0.36 Wh per 1,000 tokens is 0.77 tokens per joule.
rows.others: Plugged in, the same continuous run held 75.2 to 76.8 tok/s (76.1 in the table) with the GPU part at 43.8 W (nvidia-smi) against 30.3 W on battery. The same review ran the MacBook Pro 14 M5 Pro through the same test on battery: 68.1 tok/s at 60 to 65 W (0.27 Wh per 1,000 tokens), not added here.
rows.src_name: Frandroid, Nvidia RTX Spark review (Asus ProArt P16), 2026-10-15
